name: cold_nopressure_v1
hypothesis: For installers whose own website promises no pressure selling (~223), an opener that names that promise and answers it ('one polite check-in, no pressure') gets more positive replies than the standard opener, because it removes their first objection: chasing homeowners clashes with how they sell.
variable: opening paragraphs only (the homeowner text, offer line, ask and follow-up 2 identical to cold_offer_v1 arm A)
decision_rule: Directional only: the whole segment is ~223, so ~110 per arm. Keep the tailored opener if it has >= 80% probability of the higher positive-reply rate AND no more opt-outs than control; then reuse the 'name their stated objection' pattern for other segments.

arms.subject: last year's quotes
arms.body:
Hi,

Your site promises no pressure selling. Good: nothing I send is pushy.

I'd text the ones {company} quoted last year, from your name:

"Hi, it's {company}. We quoted for your windows a while back. Did you ever get that sorted?"

Anyone still keen goes in your diary. You only pay for surveys that get booked.

Worth a go?

sequence_note: 2 emails per company (decided 2026-10-11): email 1 + follow-up 2 at +3 business days; follow-up 3 is never sent.
